name: dash-mpd-cli
desc: Download media content from a DASH-MPEG or DASH-WebM MPD manifest
why: Downloads DASH streams from manifests, a window into how adaptive video is actually assembled.

brief.what_it_is: A command-line application, written in Rust and MIT-licensed, that downloads audio or video described by a DASH MPD manifest. Input is an MPD URL. It selects the best-matching alternative by bitrate, codec and similar criteria, fetches the segments over HTTP, HTTPS or HTTP/2, and muxes audio and video together using an external tool (mkvmerge, ffmpeg, VLC or MP4Box). It can also download subtitles in WebVTT, TTML, SRT, tx3g, SMIL and wvtt. Output is a local media file, with the container chosen from the output filename extension (for example .mp4, .mkv or .webm).
brief.why_it_exists: The author built it to watch a news programme from a public broadcaster's replay service at the gym, where the network was sometimes poor. The README frames it as a way to download streaming video or audio for local use, and it builds on the dash-mpd-rs library.
brief.how_it_works: It parses the MPD XML and chooses a representation by bitrate, codec, language, resolution, stream id and role. It then requests the media segments over HTTP(S) and calls an external muxer to combine them. The muxer is picked by output extension, in a preference order: for .mkv, mkvmerge then ffmpeg then MP4Box; for .mp4, ffmpeg then VLC then MP4Box; for .webm, VLC then ffmpeg. A --muxer-preference option overrides this order.

brief.install_notes: Prebuilt binaries are on GitHub releases for Linux AMD64 (static musl), Windows AMD64 and macOS aarch64. Alternatives are cargo install or a container image at ghcr.io/emarsden/dash-mpd-cli (about 220 MB, Podman or Docker, multiarch including arm64, armv7 and riscv64). The README treats the container as the safest route because it bundles every helper. Native installs need external tools depending on use: mkvmerge (MKVToolNix) for .mkv; ffmpeg or VLC for .mp4; MP4Box (GPAC) optionally for wvtt subtitles and as a fallback muxer; mp4decrypt (Bento4) or shaka-packager for DRM; xsltproc for MPD rewriting. Non-standard install locations can be given with flags such as --ffmpeg-location, --vlc-location, --mkvmerge-location, --mp4box-location, --mp4decrypt-location and --shaka-packager-location. No account is mentioned.
brief.standout: Compared with yt-dlp, ffmpeg, VLC or streamlink, the README claims it handles multi-period manifests, XLink elements and xHE-AAC audio that those tools reportedly fail on. It can also read cookies from installed browsers, add Basic or Bearer auth for both manifest and CDN, and rewrite the MPD with a user XSLT stylesheet before downloading.
brief.status: unknown. The GitHub README shows a CI badge, a crates.io badge, a deps.rs dependency-status badge and a published container image, which suggests active upkeep. I did not see a release date or last-commit date on either page, so I cannot confirm recency.
brief.caveats: Live (dynamic) MPD streams are not really supported. Pseudo-live streams work with --enable-live-streams, and --sleep-requests may help with live. Not supported: HLS m3u8, XLink with actuate=onRequest, and Microsoft Smooth Streaming. DRM decryption needs mp4decrypt or shaka-packager installed plus a key via --key. Android (termux), FreeBSD and OpenBSD need the cookies feature disabled, and OpenBSD support for the external decryptors is poor. Static musl builds do not work with OpenSSL, so they use rustls, which can fail some handshakes. The README warns that redistributing media you did not produce may breach IP law and that circumventing DRM may be prohibited in some countries.
quotes: A commandline application for downloading media content from a DASH MPD file, as used for on-demand replay of TV content and video streaming services.
dash-mpd-cli is written in the Rust programming language, meaning that it’s high performance and protected from a variety of vulnerabilities that can affect more traditional software.

The author is not the morality police nor a lawyer, but please note that redistributing media content that you have not produced may, depending on the publication licence, be a breach of intellectual property laws.
